provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of jss two work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list civic rights and duties, explain the importance of civic education.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about community development and leadership. Today we will revise what makes us good citizens.
Content:
Rights are freedoms given to citizens like right to education and vote. Duties are responsibilities like paying taxes and obeying laws. For example, as students your duty is to respect teachers and right is to learn in safe classroom. Rights protect you while duties keep society orderly.
Class activity:
Quick quiz in pairs: students take turns naming one right and one duty.
Evaluation questions:
What is the difference between rights and duties? Name two civic rights. What happens if citizens don't perform their duties? Why are rights important?
Summary:
Rights and duties work together to make good citizenship.

topics.title: The constitution
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define constitution, list sources of Nigerian constitution.
Introduction:
Last week we discussed rights and duties. Today we learn the document that protects these rights - the constitution.
Content:
Constitution is the supreme law of a land. Sources include written documents like 1999 Nigerian Constitution, customs, court judgments and international agreements. Our constitution has sections on fundamental rights, structure of government and how laws are made. It's like the rulebook for our country.
Class activity:
Students identify sections of the constitution in groups and explain their importance.
Evaluation questions:
What is a constitution? List three sources of Nigerian constitution. Why is constitution called supreme law? How does constitution protect citizens?
Summary:
The constitution is the foundation of our legal system and protects citizens' rights.

topics.title: Features of the Nigerian constitution
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify key sections of Nigerian constitution, explain their importance.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about constitutions in general. Today we focus specifically on what makes our Nigerian constitution special.
Content:
Key sections include: Fundamental Rights (Chapter IV), Structure of Government (Parts I-IV), Citizenship and Federal Character. The Fundamental Rights section protects freedom of speech, religion and movement. Like when a market trader speaks against bad policies, their right to expression is protected. Federal Character ensures fair representation from all regions.
Class activity:
Case talks: students discuss real situations where constitutional rights were applied or violated.
Evaluation questions:
Name three key sections of Nigerian constitution. How does the constitution protect freedom of speech? What is federal character principle? Why is citizenship important in constitution?
Summary:
The Nigerian constitution's features work together to ensure justice and fairness for all citizens.

topics.title: Democracy and its pillars
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain democracy, identify its key pillars.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about our constitution. Today we explore how our government operates under democracy.
Content:
Democracy is government by the people, for the people. Key pillars are: Rule of Law (everyone equal before law), Participation (citizens vote and join political parties), Free and Fair Elections, Protection of Rights, and Accountability. Like when citizens vote for their class representative, they participate in democracy. Rule of law means even the president must obey traffic laws.
Class activity:
Class democracy: students elect class officers following democratic procedures.
Evaluation questions:
What is democracy? Name three pillars of democracy. How does participation strengthen democracy? Why is rule of law important? What happens when leaders are not accountable?
Summary:
Democracy works when citizens actively participate and leaders follow the rule of law.

topics.title: Nationalism
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define nationalism, identify contributions of founding fathers.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about democracy. Today we explore love for country and those who fought for our independence.
Content:
Nationalism is love and loyalty to one's country. Our founding fathers included Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo and Ahmadu Bello. They fought against colonial rule through protests and negotiations. Azikiwe promoted education, Awolowo developed Western Region, Bello united Northern Nigeria. Their work helped create the Nigeria we have today.
Class activity:
Nationalist profiles: students research and present contributions of one founding father.
Evaluation questions:
What is nationalism? Name three Nigerian founding fathers. How did nationalism help gain independence? What contributions did Azikiwe make? Why are founding fathers important?
Summary:
Nationalism unites us as Nigerians and inspires us to build our country together.

topics.title: Responsible parenthood
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list duties of parents, explain family values.
Introduction:
Last week we discussed nationalism. Today we explore family responsibilities that build strong citizens.
Content:
Duties of parents include providing food, shelter, education and moral guidance. Family values like honesty, respect and hard work are passed from parents to children. For example, a parent teaching child to tell the truth builds honesty. Parents also prepare children for society like teaching market trader's child about customer service.
Class activity:
Students discuss family values in their homes and how they help build good citizens.
Evaluation questions:
Name three duties of parents. What are family values? How do parents prepare children for society? Why is education important for children? What happens when parents neglect duties?
Summary:
Responsible parenthood builds strong families that create good citizens for our nation.

topics.title: Civil society
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define civil society, identify groups that serve the public.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about family responsibilities. Today we explore organizations that help communities outside government.
Content:
Civil society includes organizations like trade unions, religious groups, NGOs and community associations that serve public interest. For example, Red Cross helps during disasters, teachers unions improve education, market associations support traders. These groups fill gaps in government services and give citizens voice in decision-making.
Class activity:
Join a cause: students identify a local issue and propose how civil society can help solve it.
Evaluation questions:
What is civil society? Name three examples in Nigeria. How do civil society groups help communities? Why are civil societies important? What can students do to join civil society?
Summary:
Civil society organizations strengthen communities by addressing needs and giving citizens a voice.

topics.title: Public opinion
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define public opinion, explain its importance in democracy.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about civil society. Today we explore how people's views shape our democracy.
Content:
Public opinion is the collective view of citizens on issues. It influences government decisions like when government listens to protests about fuel prices. In Harmattan season, public opinion about air quality can lead to environmental policies. Media helps form public opinion through news reports and social media.
Class activity:
Class poll: students vote on a school issue and discuss how their opinion represents public opinion.
Evaluation questions:
What is public opinion? How does public opinion influence government? What role does media play in forming public opinion? Why is public opinion important in democracy? How do citizens express public opinion?
Summary:
Public opinion helps leaders understand what citizens want and make better decisions.

topics.title: Voting and elections
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain voting process, identify importance of PVC.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about public opinion. Today we explore how citizens express their opinions through voting.
Content:
Voting is choosing leaders or deciding issues. In Nigeria, we use Permanent Voter Cards (PVC) to vote. The process includes registering, getting PVC, voting at polling stations and counting votes. Like when students vote for class captain, each vote counts. PVC proves your identity and prevents multiple voting.
Class activity:
Mock voting: students register, get PVC and vote for class officers following election procedures.
Evaluation questions:
What is voting? Why is PVC important in elections? What happens during election day? How does voting strengthen democracy? What are election offences?
Summary:
Voting is our right and duty to choose leaders who represent our interests.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer past questions, identify common exam topics.
Introduction:
This week we will revise all topics and practice for our final exam.
Content:
We will review key concepts like constitution, democracy, nationalism, responsible parenthood, civil society, public opinion and voting. Past questions from BECE will be discussed to understand exam patterns. Students will mark and correct answers to improve their understanding.
Class activity:
Group work: students create mind maps of all topics covered this term.
Evaluation questions:
Explain three features of Nigerian constitution. What are pillars of democracy? How does nationalism build unity? Why is responsible parenthood important? How do civil societies help communities?
Summary:
Regular revision helps us remember important concepts for our exams and future citizenship.
